## Proposition 6.25
**Statement:** To construct one and the same figure similar to a given rectilineal figure and equal to another given rectilineal figure.

**Step 1.** Let F be the given rectilineal figure to which the required figure must be similar, and G the given rectilineal figure to which it must be equal. Choose a side a of F. Construct squares Q and R equal in area to F and G respectively, and denote their sides by p and q. [2.14]

**Step 2.** To the three straight lines p, q, a construct a fourth proportional b, so that
p : q = a : b. [6.12]

**Step 3.** On b construct a rectilineal figure H similar and similarly situated to F, with b corresponding to the side a of F. [6.18]

**Step 4.** The squares Q and R are similar: their corresponding angles are equal because all are right angles, and their sides about equal angles are proportional because each square has all its sides equal. [D1.22, P4, D5.5, D6.1] Regard them as similarly described on p and q. Thus Q and R are similar figures described on p and q, while F and H are similar and similarly described on a and b. Since p : q = a : b, it follows that
Q : R = F : H. [6.22]
The direct ratio-transfer proposition 6.22 is the natural choice here because the construction has supplied precisely its four proportional straight lines and two pairs of similar figures.

**Step 5.** Substituting Q = F and R = G into this proportion gives
F : G = F : H. [D5.5]
Magnitudes to which the same magnitude has the same ratio are equal; therefore G = H. [5.9] By Step 3, H is also similar to F. Hence the one figure H is similar to the given rectilineal figure F and equal to the other given rectilineal figure G, as required. [6.18, 5.9]

heath_proof_text: Let ABC be the given rectilineal figure to which the figure to be constructed must be similar, and D that to which it must be equal; thus it is required to construct one and the same figure similar to ABC and equal to D. Let there be applied to BC the parallelogram BE equal to the triangle ABC [I. 44], and to CE the parallelogram CM equal to D in the angle FCE which is equal to the angle CBL. [I. 45] Therefore BC is in a straight line with CF, and LE with EM. Now let GH be taken a mean proportional to BC, CF [VI. 13], and on GH let KGH be described similar and similarly situated to ABC. [VI. 18] Then, since, as BC is to GH, so is GH to CF, and, if three straight lines be proportional, as the first is to the third, so is the figure on the first to the similar and similarly situated figure described on the second, [VI. 19] therefore, as BC is to CF, so is the triangle ABC to the triangle KGH. But, as BC is to CF, so also is the parallelogram BE to the parallelogram EF. [VI. 1] Therefore also, as the triangle ABC is to the triangle KGH, so is the parallelogram BE to the parallelogram EF; therefore, alternately, as the triangle ABC is to the parallelogram BE, so is the triangle KGH to the parallelogram EF. [V. 16] But the triangle ABC is equal to the parallelogram BE; therefore the triangle KGH is also equal to the parallelogram EF. But the parallelogram EF is equal to D; therefore KGH is also equal to D. And KGH is also similar to ABC. Therefore one and the same figure KGH has been constructed similar to the given rectilineal figure ABC and equal to the other given figure D.
